messages:
incident-bot: Pager alert: HIGH - apigw.edge requests 5xx spike (502/504) in us-west-2 · affected p50/p95 latency · link: https://metrics.redwood.internal/d/edge/apigw?panel=503
incident-bot: Severity: P1 · triggered by rate(5xx) > 5% over 1m · suggested runbook: https://wiki.redwood.internal/runbooks/apigw-5xx
oncall-ryan: acked. I'm on it. Starting quick triage — assigning SRE and runtime.
oncall-ryan: Observed: spike started ~09:12 UTC, 5xx ~18% now in us-west-2. Error mix ~= 60% 502, 35% 504, rest 500/timeouts. Upstream latency for some backends increased to 2–4s.
sre-ana: I'm collecting edge proxy logs + nginx error samples. Pulling recent deploys, but CI shows no rollout in last 2h. Running a quick curl to the edge gateway from prod canary:
```
curl -v -H 'Host: api.redwood.com' 'https://edge-usw2-01.redwood/api/health' -o /tmp/edge-health.txt
cat /tmp/edge-health.txt | tail -n 50
```
sre-ana: Also dumping proxy connection reset / upstream timeout traces now.
eng-runtime-marc: No runtime deploys pushed in last 3h from my side. I saw a config change to the edge route table at 08:55 for an A/B routing rule (traffic-split) — @netops-sam you own the LB changes, can you confirm?
netops-sam: I rolled a small NLB route tweak at 08:55 to add a new weight rule for canary, but it was only metadata (no target changes). I did restart the edge-proxy service on a subset of nodes for a cert rotation at 08:58 — might correlate. Checking logs.
support-lead-jyoti: Support is seeing incoming tickets from multiple enterprise customers starting at 09:13. Top impacted customers: cust_0192, cust_1139, cust_enterprise_acme — roughly 15–30% request failures for them. I'm drafting a status message for customers.
pm-lena: Are any SLAs at risk? Please surface enterprise impact ASAP. Notify account execs if >20% failure for >10m.
oncall-ryan: Quick mitigation plan: 1) pause the A/B traffic split -> route all traffic to stable pool 2) increase proxy upstream timeout from 2s -> 6s 3) temporarily enable circuit-breaker to reject heavy fanout requests 4) shift 30% traffic to us-east-1 as fallback. Executing step 1 now.
oncall-ryan: step1 done — paused canary, traffic to stable pool. Error rate dipped slightly to 14% in 30s.
eng-runtime-marc: I'm preparing a rollback for the certificate restart nodes — will roll them back from the restarted pool to healthy config.
sre-ana: Running a targeted curl to upstream to see the 502 path:
```
# from edge node
curl -s -D - -o /dev/null 'http://upstream-usw2-03.internal:8080/route/check' -w '%{http_code} %{time_total}\n'
```
sre-ana: upstream responses show intermittent 499/504 from upstream app instances and many tcp FINs from connection pool exhaustion on some proxy workers. Looks like keepalive connection exhaustion with increased short-lived connections.
netops-sam: If connection pool exhausted, increasing keepalive or lowering max_conns per worker might help short-term. I'm going to bump proxy keepalive and recycle a small subset of proxies (rolling) to avoid full fanout.
eng-runtime-marc: Rolling a config change to increase proxy keepalive to 120s and reduce max workers spawn. Applying to one cluster now.
support-lead-jyoti: Customer comms sent to accounts with high impact. Support queue: 28 new tickets in 10m. Escalating to enterprise success for Acme.
incident-bot: Update posted to incident channel and incident timeline. Metrics show slow improvement after pause + keepalive bump. 5xx down from 18% -> 8% in 3m.
oncall-ryan: Initiating step 4: shift 30% traffic to us-east-1 via traffic-router CLI:
```
infra traffic-router set-weight --service apigw --region us-east-1 --weight 30
```
oncall-ryan: shift done. Latency p95 normalized in us-west for stable pool; global 5xx now 4.2%.
pm-lena: Good — please prepare a brief for execs with timeline and customer list. Also schedule a follow-up postmortem meeting.
sre-ana: Root cause hypothesis: combination of a rolling restart (cert rotation) that transiently reduced pool capacity + connection keepalive/configuration that caused connection churn -> upstream timeouts and 502s. We'll confirm with more evidence from proxy metrics.
eng-runtime-marc: Action items I'm taking: 1) revert the restart-induced node pool (restore full capacity) 2) add connection pooling metrics to dashboards 3) ship a short-term circuit breaker for high-fanout routes.
netops-sam: Long-term: we'll add an automated pre-rolling health-check that prevents node restarts if pool concurrency already high.
support-lead-jyoti: Current customer impact: impacting ~6% of global requests for ~18m window; 4 enterprise customers saw >20% for 12m. We escalated and offered temporary credits.
incident-bot: Incident state: mitigated -> residual errors trending to baseline. Postmortem requested; severity = P1 -> follow-up meeting scheduled.
oncall-ryan: Marking this thread for handoff to postmortem. Thanks all for quick coordination. Will update when the final postmortem is created. :white_check_mark:
